name: IOC - Judgment Panda attacks: APT31 today
description:
APT31 is a cyberespionage group focused on industrial espionage and theft of intellectual property. The group disguises its tools as legitimate software and abuses legitimate online services to establish bidirectional C2 channels for its malware.

From 2024 to 2025, Russia's IT sector — particularly contractors and systems integrators serving government agencies — was hit by a series of targeted cyberattacks. What made these attacks stand out was the attackers' well-planned tactics, which let them stay undetected for a long time. While investigating the incidents, we were able to link some of the attacks to APT31, reconstruct the group's tactics and techniques, and obtain unique samples of its tools.

name: Salt Typhoon: A Persistent Threat to Global Telecommunications Infrastructure
Raging Panda Attacks: APT31 Today
description:
APT31, a cyber espionage group focusing on industrial theft and intellectual property, has recently targeted the Russian IT sector, employing sophisticated techniques and a variety of malware. The threat actor utilizes cloud services, particularly Russian platforms, as command-and-control (C2) mechanisms, enhancing their ability to operate covertly.

Their initial access was achieved through compromised infrastructure, beginning as early as late 2022. A notable method employed was the use of spear-phishing techniques to gain footholds, with crafted attachments that deployed malware like CloudyLoader. The attackers leverage prepared scripts for lateral movement within the networks, utilizing tools such as Impacket's WmiExec, SmbExec, and Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) for privileged access and system control.

name: APT15 Cyber Espionage: Campaigns and TTPs Analysis
description: APT15, a cyber espionage group with origins in China, has been active since approximately 2010 and has conducted numerous high-profile campaigns targeting government, diplomatic, and military sectors across North America, Europe, and the Middle East. Their operations include notable incidents such as the 2013 "moviestar" operation against European Ministries of Foreign Affairs, attacks on Indian embassy personnel in 2016, and the hacking of a US Navy contractor in 2018. Even after significant disruptions like the 2021 crackdown by Microsoft, APT15 adapted and continued its activities, notably deploying a new backdoor called Graphican in 2022 and using the ORB3 network for operations in 2023.
